newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.S. envoy to press Bosnian elections plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to press Bosnian elections plan.

text.p: U.S. envoy John Kornblum is due to Sarajevo on Monday to hold talks with Serb, Croat and Moslem leaders and try to end a dispute over municipal elections in Bosnia, Western officials said on Sunday.

Kornblum is leading a diplomatic drive by major powers to ensure the politically-sensitive elections go ahead as planned on November 23 and 24, despite a vow by Bosnian Serb authorities not to take part.
Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic said on Friday that the international community had asked too many concessions of the Serbs and they would not hold the municipal polls on their territory.
Bosnia's rival nationalist parties view the municipal elections, which follow national polls for a presidency and parliament on September 14, as a political battleground over disputed territory.
Serb authorities fear they could be voted of power by Moslem refugees who registered to vote in their former home towns.
Envoys from Britain, France, Germany and Russia were expected to join Kornblum's effort to salvage the local elections and breathe life into the post-war governing bodies, the local media reported.
The reports said Kornblum also intended to press Moslem, Croat and Serb leaders to speed up work by Bosnia's newly-elected collective presidency and parliament.
The presidency has only met once and Serb deputies boycotted the inaugural session of the parliament this month.
